input: Enroll in an online astronomy course for beginners

keyUnknowns.whyItMatters: Astronomy is broad — knowing whether the user wants general sky-watching, astrophysics theory, telescope use, or a specific topic (e.g. planets, cosmology) completely changes which courses to recommend.
There are free, freemium, and paid courses ranging from $0 to hundreds of dollars; budget determines which options are even on the table.
Some courses are self-paced and open-ended; others run on fixed weekly schedules. The user's available hours per week and total time commitment window shapes the shortlist.
The user may already have a subscription (Coursera, edX, Udemy, YouTube, etc.) or a strong preference for a specific learning platform, which narrows the search immediately.
If the user needs a verifiable certificate (for a CV, academic application, or personal milestone) versus just learning for fun, this filters courses that offer formal credentials vs. informal ones.
Some learners thrive with video lectures, others prefer reading-heavy or interactive/quiz-based formats; matching format to style determines satisfaction and completion.
Knowing what 'done well' means — e.g. finishing all modules, being able to identify constellations, passing a final exam, or simply staying enrolled — defines the target and how to measure progress.

gold.taskTitle: Enroll in a beginner online astronomy course
gold.taskDescription: Find and sign up for an online astronomy course suited to a complete beginner.

questions.title: Which astronomy topic interests you most right now?
questions.description: Identify the specific area of astronomy the user wants to focus on — e.g. general stargazing, planets and the solar system, deep-space cosmology, telescope operation, or astrophysics theory.

questions.title: What is your budget for this course?
questions.description: Determine whether the user wants a free course, is open to a one-time paid purchase, or is willing to take on a monthly subscription platform.

questions.title: How many hours per week can you dedicate to studying?
questions.description: Understand the user's available time commitment so courses can be matched to realistic workload expectations (e.g. 1–2 hrs/week vs. 5–10 hrs/week).

questions.title: Do you have a preferred learning platform already?
questions.description: Find out if the user already uses or subscribes to a platform like Coursera, edX, Udemy, Khan Academy, or YouTube, to prioritize courses available there.

questions.title: Do you need an official certificate upon completion?
questions.description: Clarify whether the user requires a verifiable, shareable certificate — for a resume, academic portfolio, or personal record — or is enrolling purely for personal enrichment.

questions.title: How do you learn best — videos, reading, or interactive quizzes?
questions.description: Identify the user's preferred content format so the recommended course matches their learning style and maximizes engagement and completion likelihood.

questions.title: What will completing this course mean to you?
questions.description: Define what a successful outcome looks like — finishing all modules, gaining practical stargazing skills, passing an assessment, or simply exploring a new hobby — to set a clear goal.
